newsitem.title: ITALY: SOCCER-MILAN PUSH JUVENTUS CLOSER TO TITLE.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-MILAN PUSH JUVENTUS CLOSER TO TITLE.

text.p: Juventus stretched their Italian serie A lead to six points on Thursday, thrashing lowly Piacenza 4-1 and almost killing off the hopes of second-placed Parma who were held 1-1 by outgoing champions AC Milan.
The results meant that, with three matches remaining, Parma must beat European Cup holders Juventus in their clash in Turin on Sunday to keep their dreams alive.

Even that may not be enough and they must look warily over their shoulders at UEFA Cup finalists Inter, who moved to within two points of Parma in third place after beating relegated Reggiana 3-1 in Milan.
Parma had looked on course to cut the gap when striker Enrico Chiesa scored in the sixth minute. They led 1-0 at the break while Juventus were drawing 0-0 with Piacenza.
But Demetrio Albertini calmly levelled the score for the troubled champions with a 70th minute penalty after Stefano Eranio was felled in the area.
French midfielder Zinedine Zidane, who replaced surprise starter Alessandro Del Piero at halftime, brought Juventus alive with a 51st minute goal.
Italy striker Christian Vieri scored twice and Vladimir Jugovic provided another in a second-half rout.
Pasquale Luiso had briefly given Piacenza hope in the 55th minute to cut the deficit to 2-1.
